lessons: Contrary to the guide's 56% WR, my WR went 0-6 in games: 6 Mountains were too few for Brimstone Volley, Traitorous Blood and Curse of the Pierced Heart, so count red pips.
My WR had only three fliers (Abbey Griffin, Chapel Geist, Spectral Rider) and lost all six games in 17-29 turns; take a fourth flier over Silverchase Fox or a second Thraben Purebloods.
The guide says take cheap threats over filler, yet my Unruly Mob and two Thraben Purebloods were ground filler in an 0-3 WR; prefer Claustrophobia-style removal or a flier.

Don't take a slow self-mill shell without enough fast pressure: my UB deck won 1-2 with Victim of Night, Dead Weight and Corpse Lunge, but games ran 16 to 22 turns, so draft more cheap threats than Snapcaster Mage.

Draft instant-speed answers to fliers early: Round 2's UR and Round 3's WU both pressured me in the air with Stitched Drake, Midnight Haunting and Invisible Stalker, and I had too few answers to them.
Don't wait on a sideboard swap: I brought in six cards before game 2 against UR and lost anyway, so settle the 23 in the main deck by Pack 3 instead.
Fliers held up: Midnight Haunting tokens and two Invisible Stalkers closed both 2-0 wins, matching the guide's fliers-win advice, and Moorland Haunt worked as a 17th land.
The 1-2 loss to UR dragged to 17-24 turns, so prize cheap early attackers and Blazing Torch over slow filler to close games faster.
The guide calls Delver of Secrets weak, and I cut both Delvers, yet I took them over playables; pass them for removal or two-drop creatures.
Draft red aggression early: the 3-0 deck was built on two Geistflame (the second came in pack 3), Rage Thrower and red creatures, with burn clearing blockers for pressure.
Expect grindy games: they ran 17–24 turns, so prioritise evasive finishers like Stitched Drake and Battleground Geist over marginal ground creatures.
Blue worked as a light second colour: five blue cards ran on six Islands plus Sulfur Falls, so commit to red and take blue only when it's open.
Sensory Deprivation was my first pick in pack 1 and again in pack 3, yet my BR never played blue; the guide's advice to take it early cost two picks, so commit by pick 5.
Furor of the Bitten is a pump, not removal as my notes said; my 1-2 loss to RG had only Harvest Pyre and Corpse Lunge as real removal, so take removal over ground creatures.
Two of tonight's BR wins ended in 9 and 17 turns, contradicting the guide's claim that ground BR stalls; fast starts beat slow boards, so keep early drops.
Settle colours earlier: my pack 2 black picks (Victim of Night, Abattoir Ghoul, Diregraf Ghoul) all got cut, while red top end like Into the Maw of Hell carried RG.
Prioritise cheap blockers and reach over extra top end: RG's expensive threats stalled in the 24- and 25-turn games against WB's fliers in round 2.
Draft more answers to fliers early: WB's Chapel Geist pair and Screeching Bat decided the grindy games I lost in round 2.
Cobbled Wings, which the guide says to skip, made my main deck and I sided it out for Sharpened Pitchfork before game 2 of round 1, so take a real body over it at pick 13.
I spent picks 13 and 14 of pack 3 on Think Twice, which never made my deck, while Walking Corpse, filler by the guide, was my 23rd card, so take playable creatures over card-draw spells late.
The guide's flier plan only partly held: my Chapel Geist and Bloodline Keeper deck went 5-4 in games and lost 1-2 to UR's two Geistflame and Harvest Pyre, so keep a burn-resistant plan.
Draft a lower curve with more early plays: my BG deck, top-heavy with Boneyard Wurm, Lumberknot and two Prey Upon, stalled and lost 1-2, 0-2 and 0-2 in games lasting 15 to 26 turns.

Prioritize flying defense over white fliers you won't play: my Angel of Flight Alabaster and Abbey Griffin picks went unused, while opponents' Chapel Geist, Falkenrath Noble and Vampire Interloper flyers went unanswered in my BG deck.
Cut the marginal Make a Wish copy I had flagged for cutting: I kept it in a 23-spell deck that never closed games quickly, so filler slots should yield to proactive creatures.
